principle.name: Human-Readable Specifications
principle.description: Specs should be readable by humans without technical testing knowledge. Focus on user behavior and outcomes, not implementation details.
principle.rationale: Specs serve as communication between product owners and test engineers.

example.good:
Steps: 1. Enter valid username and password 2. Click Sign In button
Expected Results: - User is redirected to dashboard - Welcome message is displayed

principle.name: Comprehensive Coverage
principle.description: Cover all acceptance criteria including positive, negative, and edge cases.
principle.rationale: Complete test coverage prevents regressions and ensures quality.

principle.name: Seed Test Reference
principle.description: Reference the seed test in specs to provide patterns for the generator.
principle.rationale: Seed tests demonstrate test structure, fixtures, and patterns.

convention.rule: Use lowercase with hyphens for word separation
Include both happy path and error cases

pitfall.why_problematic: Tests only verify happy path, missing error handling validation.
pitfall.correct_approach: Always include error scenarios: invalid input, network failures, permissions.

pitfall.why_problematic: Specs become implementation details, not user behavior descriptions.
pitfall.correct_approach: Describe what the user does and sees, not how to automate it.

pitfall.why_problematic: Tests may pass but not verify correct behavior.
pitfall.correct_approach: Be specific about what should be visible, what data should change.

category.name: before_starting
category.item: Understand user story and acceptance criteria

category.name: during_creation
category.item: Include positive, negative, and edge cases

category.name: before_completion
category.item: Check scenarios are clear and actionable
